meta.move: Skill: cites procedure 4.4 correctly after owning the call
meta.expect: Says 4.4 meets her fallback demand, flatly, wants it in writing; does NOT move to the last position on 4.4 alone; debrief Where she ended says whether that is the fair outcome

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided, and when?
Before anything: I entered the zero before calling you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Now tell me what it was based on.

I want to read you section 4.4. For a first concern, the student may complete a supervised reassessment. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the original and nothing is placed in his record. This is a first concern.
That's 4.4, and the part about nothing on his record I'll want in writing tonight. But a rewrite for what? You still haven't shown me anything.
I'll commit to that in writing tonight: nothing goes on his record.
Tonight. Good. Now the zero, and what you based it on.
So will you agree to the rewrite?
No. Agreeing to a rewrite before you've shown me a single thing would be admitting something, and I'm not doing that.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed in our meeting to confirm in writing that nothing will be placed in Owen's record. I still expect the zero withdrawn, and I expect to see whatever you based it on. I expect that confirmation in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Fallback position; she has your commitment that nothing goes on his record, and she still wants the zero withdrawn and to see what it was based on. The fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was not reached because no evidence was ever put in front of her.
What moved her: You cited the reassessment procedure correctly and committed in writing to keeping it off his record, which met the one thing she would never give up.
What cost ground: You asked her to agree to the rewrite before showing anything, and taking it then would have meant admitting something about her son.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your case never came near that night because you showed no evidence at all; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked what the zero was based on, answer with one dated, specific document tied to Owen's own work that she can check herself, and only then offer the rewrite.
